The Direct Connect gateway advertises the prefix with a longer AS path than the VPN, so the transit gateway selects the shorter AS path of the VPN
The transit gateway keeps the previous best path until the BGP hold timer of the Direct Connect session has expired twice after it recovered

stem: A dedicated Direct Connect connection carries four private VIFs for production VPCs. The team wants to raise the MTU of one VIF to 9001 for a replication workload. The connection has never been used with jumbo frames. What should the team plan for this change?

choices.text: A new VIF must be created with jumbo frames enabled, because the MTU of an existing private VIF cannot be changed after creation
Only the VIF being changed renegotiates BGP, so the change can be made during business hours without affecting the other three VIFs
The change is applied by AWS during the next scheduled maintenance of the Direct Connect location, so no maintenance window is required
Updating the connection can briefly disrupt all VIFs on it for up to about 30 seconds, so the change belongs in a maintenance window

stem: A network team sends VPC Flow Logs for a shared services VPC to CloudWatch Logs. The team wants a continuously updated view of the top 10 source IP addresses by rejected packets and by bytes, without running ad hoc queries or building a separate analytics pipeline. Which solution fits?

choices.text: Export the flow log group to Amazon S3 each day and use Athena with a GROUP BY query on source address to produce the top 10 table
Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule on the flow log group, keyed on source address and filtered on the REJECT action, and add it to a dashboard
Run a CloudWatch Logs Insights query every hour from an EventBridge schedule and store the top 10 results as JSON objects in an S3 bucket
Create a metric filter for each known source IP address in the flow log group and plot the resulting metrics together on one CloudWatch dashboard

stem: A network account owns a transit gateway with 60 VPC attachments from 25 application accounts plus two VPN attachments. The network team wants to analyze traffic volume between attachments and see packets dropped because of missing routes, without asking every application team to enable anything in their accounts. Which option fits best?

choices.text: Use an AWS Config rule that requires every application account to enable VPC Flow Logs on all VPC attachment ENIs of the transit gateway
Enable Traffic Mirroring on the transit gateway attachments and send the mirrored packets to an analysis appliance in the network account
Create Transit Gateway Flow Logs on the transit gateway in the network account and publish them to Amazon S3 for analysis with Athena
Use Reachability Analyzer from the network account to test every pair of attachments and export each analysis result to Amazon S3

stem: An Application Load Balancer in front of Node.js targets returns occasional HTTP 502 errors under light load. ALB access logs show elb_status_code 502 with target_status_code "-" for these requests. The ALB idle timeout is 60 seconds, and the Node.js HTTP server uses its default keep-alive timeout of 5 seconds. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: Targets close idle keep-alive connections before the ALB does, so the ALB reuses a closed connection; set target keep-alive above the ALB idle timeout
The ALB idle timeout is too short for slow requests, so it closes connections mid-response; increase the ALB idle timeout to 300 seconds
The targets are running out of memory and returning 502 themselves; add instances to the target group and enable slow start mode
The target group health check interval is too long, so unhealthy targets receive traffic; shorten the interval and lower the unhealthy threshold

stem: Application servers keep idle TCP connections to a database fleet behind a Network Load Balancer. After about six minutes without traffic, the next query on a connection fails, and CloudWatch shows TCP_ELB_Reset_Count increasing. Which TWO actions resolve the problem? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Switch the target group health check to HTTP so the NLB can detect idle connections and refresh them before they time out
Enable cross-zone load balancing on the NLB so that idle connections can be moved to a target in another Availability Zone
Enable TCP keepalives on the application servers with an interval shorter than the NLB TCP idle timeout so connections never look idle
Enable connection draining with a longer deregistration delay on the target group so idle connections are kept open for longer
Increase the TCP idle timeout on the NLB listener to a value longer than the longest expected idle period of the connections

stem: A software company lets customers worldwide download installers of 200 MB to 2 GB directly from public S3 bucket URLs. Data transfer out is now the largest line on the bill, and customers far from the bucket's Region report slow downloads. Which TWO changes lower cost and improve download speed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket so that download charges move from the company to the customers who download the files
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and publish the accelerated endpoint URLs to customers for all installer downloads
Replicate the bucket to every Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication and let customers choose the nearest regional bucket URL
Serve the downloads through a CloudFront distribution with the bucket as an origin, because transfer from S3 to CloudFront is not charged
Use a CloudFront cache policy with long TTLs for the versioned installers so repeat downloads are served from edge caches near customers

stem: On-premises DNS servers forward queries for AWS private zones to a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint with two IP addresses. During nightly batch jobs, some queries time out, and the endpoint's CloudWatch metrics show query volume near the documented per-address capacity. Which change improves reliability?

choices.text: Enable DNSSEC validation on the Route 53 Resolver for the VPC so that malformed queries are rejected earlier and reduce the load on the endpoint
Add more IP addresses to the inbound endpoint across Availability Zones and configure the on-premises forwarders to spread queries across all of them
Convert the inbound endpoint into an outbound endpoint and create forwarding rules so that the on-premises queries are resolved from inside the VPC
Increase the TTL of the records in the private hosted zones to 24 hours so that the Route 53 Resolver caches answers and handles more queries

stem: A company uses a centralized egress VPC with NAT gateways behind a transit gateway for 30 spoke VPCs. One analytics VPC now downloads about 400 TB per month from internet data providers, and its egress costs are much higher than expected. Which change most reduces cost while keeping the other spokes centralized?

choices.text: Give the analytics VPC its own NAT gateways and internet gateway, so its internet traffic no longer passes through the transit gateway at all
Add a second transit gateway dedicated to the analytics VPC and connect it to the same egress VPC so its traffic uses a separate attachment
Replace the NAT gateways in the egress VPC with larger NAT instances so that the per-GB NAT gateway processing charge disappears for all spoke traffic
Enable appliance mode on the analytics VPC attachment so that its flows stay in one Availability Zone and avoid cross-AZ transfer inside the egress VPC

stem: A fleet of EC2 instances runs a forward proxy that opens hundreds of thousands of short-lived connections. Under peak load, clients see sporadic packet loss although CPU and bandwidth are well below limits. The ENA driver statistics show conntrack_allowance_exceeded increasing on the proxy instances. What should the team do?

choices.text: Enable Enhanced Networking with the Intel 82599 VF driver instead of ENA to remove the per-instance connection limit completely
Place the proxy instances in a cluster placement group so that all traffic stays within one rack and bypasses connection limits
Move the proxies to a larger instance size, or make the flows untracked by using security group rules that avoid connection tracking
Increase the MTU on the proxy instances to 9001 so that each packet carries more data and fewer packets need to be tracked

stem: A company reaches three VPCs (10.10.0.0/16, 10.20.0.0/16, 10.30.0.0/16) from its data center through a transit VIF, a Direct Connect gateway and a transit gateway. A fourth VPC, 10.40.0.0/16, was just attached to the transit gateway. The transit gateway route table associated with the Direct Connect gateway attachment already shows a propagated route for 10.40.0.0/16, but the on-premises router's BGP table does not contain that prefix and on-premises hosts cannot reach the new VPC. What should the network engineer change?

choices.text: Raise the prefix limit on the transit VIF BGP session, because the Direct Connect gateway stops advertising new prefixes once more than three routes are sent to on-premises
Add 10.40.0.0/16, or a summary such as 10.0.0.0/10 that covers it, to the allowed prefixes list of the association between the Direct Connect gateway and the transit gateway
Enable route propagation from the new VPC attachment into the transit gateway route table that is associated with the Direct Connect gateway attachment so BGP picks it up
Add a static route for 10.40.0.0/16 in the new VPC's subnet route tables that points to the transit gateway, so the transit gateway starts advertising the VPC over BGP

stem: A bank reaches AWS through a 1 Gbps hosted Direct Connect connection. A new regulation requires IPsec encryption for all traffic between the data center and its VPCs, and the security team forbids any public IP addresses on either end of the tunnels. The VPCs are already attached to a transit gateway. Which TWO steps implement this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable MACsec on the hosted Direct Connect connection and configure a connectivity association key on the router to encrypt the link at Layer 2 instead
Attach an accelerated Site-to-Site VPN to the transit gateway so the tunnels ride the AWS edge network and never touch public internet addresses
Create a public virtual interface and build a standard Site-to-Site VPN to the transit gateway's public tunnel endpoints over that public virtual interface
Associate a Direct Connect gateway with the transit gateway and connect it to the data center through a transit virtual interface on the hosted connection
Create a Site-to-Site VPN attached to the transit gateway with the private IPv4 outside IP address type and the Direct Connect gateway attachment as its transport

stem: A branch firewall that sits behind the building's NAT router is configured as the customer gateway for a Site-to-Site VPN. The customer gateway in AWS uses the NAT router's public IP address. The NAT router forwards UDP 500 and IP protocol 50 (ESP) to the firewall. Firewall logs show the first IKEv2 exchange completing, then no further replies from AWS, and both tunnels stay DOWN. What is the most likely fix?

choices.text: Increase the dead peer detection timeout on both tunnels, because the NAT router delays IKE packets long enough for AWS to treat the peer as dead
Recreate the customer gateway in AWS with the firewall's private IP address, because AWS must see the real device address to complete IKE authentication
Forward UDP 4500 from the NAT router to the firewall and enable NAT traversal on it, because IKE and ESP move to UDP 4500 once NAT is detected
Switch the VPN connection from dynamic BGP routing to static routing, because BGP sessions cannot be established through a device that performs NAT

stem: A company peers transit gateway TGW-A in us-east-1 (VPC 10.10.0.0/16) with TGW-B in eu-west-1 (VPC 10.20.0.0/16). Both transit gateways use their default route table for association and propagation, the peering attachment is accepted and available, and each VPC route table sends 10.0.0.0/8 to its transit gateway. Traffic between the VPCs still fails. Which TWO actions fix this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Enable route propagation for the peering attachment on both transit gateways so each side learns the other VPC CIDR dynamically
In TGW-B's default route table, add a static route for 10.10.0.0/16 that targets the inter-Region peering attachment to TGW-A
Configure a BGP session over the peering attachment with distinct ASNs on each transit gateway so routes are exchanged automatically
Add a route for the remote VPC CIDR in each VPC route table that targets the peering attachment ID instead of the local transit gateway
In TGW-A's default route table, add a static route for 10.20.0.0/16 that targets the inter-Region peering attachment to TGW-B

stem: A SaaS provider publishes its API as a PrivateLink endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer in us-east-1. A new customer runs all workloads in eu-west-1 and requires private connectivity with no VPC peering, transit gateway or internet path. The provider does not want to deploy the service stack in a second Region. What should be implemented?

choices.text: The provider creates a second Network Load Balancer in eu-west-1 with IP targets pointing to the us-east-1 instances and publishes it as a service
The customer creates an inter-Region VPC peering to a small provider VPC in us-east-1 and uses an interface endpoint there, reached across the peering
The provider places a Global Accelerator in front of the Network Load Balancer, and the customer connects to its static IP addresses from eu-west-1
The provider enables eu-west-1 as a supported Region on the endpoint service, and the customer creates an interface endpoint in eu-west-1 for that service

stem: A company runs VPCs in three Regions and wants one policy-driven global network. New VPC attachments must be placed automatically by their tag (env=prod, env=dev or env=shared). Production and development must never communicate, while both must reach the shared services VPCs. Which AWS Cloud WAN core network policy design meets these requirements?

choices.text: Segments prod, dev and shared, attachment policies that map the env tag to a segment, and segment actions that share the shared segment with prod and dev
Segments prod and dev only, with shared services VPCs attached to both segments at once so each environment can reach them through its own segment
One segment per Region that holds that Region's prod, dev and shared attachments, with route filters on the core network edges to separate the environments
One segment named global with attachments from every environment, using the isolate-attachments setting so attachments reach only shared services

stem: The networking account owns a Route 53 private hosted zone for internal.example.com. An application team must associate the zone with a VPC in its own account; both DNS resolution and DNS hostnames are already enabled on that VPC. The teams want to use native hosted zone association, not Resolver endpoints. Which TWO actions are required? (Select TWO)

choices.text: From the networking account, share the private hosted zone with the application account through AWS Resource Access Manager and accept the share
From the networking account, create a VPC association authorization for the hosted zone that names the application account's VPC ID and Region
From the application account, create a Resolver inbound endpoint and a forwarding rule for internal.example.com that targets the endpoint's addresses
From the networking account console, select the private hosted zone and add the application account's VPC ID under the zone's list of associated VPCs
From the application account, associate the VPC with the hosted zone by calling the association API with the hosted zone ID from the networking account

stem: A company has 180 VPCs in 45 accounts. Every VPC must get the same DNS setup: four private hosted zones, Resolver forwarding rules for on-premises domains, and a DNS Firewall rule group. Today a pipeline re-applies each item to each VPC separately, and drift is common. The team wants to define this DNS configuration once and apply updates everywhere. What should they implement?

choices.text: Share the Resolver rules and the DNS Firewall rule group through AWS RAM, and keep associating the private hosted zones per VPC with automation triggered by EventBridge
Deploy Resolver inbound endpoints in each VPC and have every VPC forward all queries to a central VPC that holds the zones, rules and firewall rule group instead
Create a Route 53 Profile with the zones, forwarding rules and firewall rule group, share it through AWS RAM, and associate the Profile with every VPC
Use AWS Firewall Manager with a DNS Firewall policy for the whole organization and rely on its automatic remediation to also add the hosted zones and forwarding rules

stem: A VPC is associated with a private hosted zone example.com that contains records for web.example.com and api.dev.example.com. A development team then creates a second private hosted zone, dev.example.com, with one record, app.dev.example.com, and associates it with the same VPC. Since then, instances in the VPC get NXDOMAIN for api.dev.example.com, while web.example.com still resolves. What is the cause?

choices.text: A VPC can only be associated with one private hosted zone per parent domain, so the second association silently disabled the example.com zone for dev names
The api.dev.example.com record is now cached as NXDOMAIN on each instance and the answer will return once the negative caching TTL of the zone expires
A private hosted zone cannot hold records for a subdomain name, so api.dev.example.com was never valid and only resolved from cached public DNS answers
With overlapping private zones, the Resolver answers from the most specific matching zone, dev.example.com, and does not fall back to example.com

stem: A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint forwards queries for corp.local to on-premises DNS servers. Most names resolve, but queries for a few names that return many A records or long TXT records time out. The on-premises firewall allows UDP and TCP 53 from the endpoint's IP addresses. The outbound endpoint's security group allows outbound UDP 53 to the on-premises servers only. What should be changed?

choices.text: Add an outbound rule for TCP 53 to the on-premises DNS servers in the outbound endpoint's security group, so truncated answers can be retried over TCP
Add an inbound rule for UDP 53 from the on-premises DNS servers to the outbound endpoint's security group, so large response datagrams are accepted
Raise the EDNS buffer size on the outbound endpoint in the Resolver console so that large answers fit in a single UDP response instead of being truncated
Add a third IP address in another subnet to the outbound endpoint, because large responses exceed the query capacity of the two existing IP addresses

stem: A platform team uses CloudFormation to create VPCs in 30 accounts. CIDR blocks are currently typed into template parameters from a spreadsheet, and two teams recently received overlapping ranges. The organization already runs Amazon VPC IPAM with a pool shared to all accounts. What is the simplest way for each stack to receive a unique CIDR automatically?

choices.text: Use the Fn::Cidr intrinsic function on the IPAM pool's top-level range so CloudFormation computes the next free /20 block for each new VPC stack
Add a Lambda-backed custom resource that queries the spreadsheet API, reserves the next free /20, and returns it to the VPC resource as an output value
Store the next free CIDR in a Systems Manager parameter that each stack reads through a dynamic reference and that a pipeline step increments after deploy
Set Ipv4IpamPoolId and Ipv4NetmaskLength on the AWS::EC2::VPC resource so that IPAM allocates the next free block from the pool at creation time

stem: A company's transit gateways in eu-central-1 are registered in an AWS Network Manager global network, and topology and routing changes appear in the Network Manager console. The team created an EventBridge rule in eu-central-1 with source aws.networkmanager to send transit gateway route change events to an SNS topic, but the rule never matches. What should the team do?

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail data events for the transit gateways so that route changes are recorded and then forwarded to EventBridge in the same Region as the rule
Create the EventBridge rule in us-west-2, where Network Manager publishes its events, and forward the matched events to the SNS topic or eu-central-1 bus
Turn on route analysis in the global network, because Network Manager sends routing events to EventBridge only when route analysis runs on a schedule
Change the rule's event source to aws.ec2, because transit gateway route changes are always published by the EC2 service rather than by Network Manager

stem: A CloudFormation stack defines a production VPC with CidrBlock 10.0.0.0/16. To add the range 10.1.0.0/16, an engineer edits the VPC's CidrBlock property. The change set shows the VPC with Replacement: True, which would delete every subnet and instance in it. How should the template be changed to add 10.1.0.0/16 without replacing the VPC?

choices.text: Keep CidrBlock at 10.0.0.0/16 and add a separate AWS::EC2::VPCCidrBlock resource for 10.1.0.0/16, with new subnets depending on that resource
Attach a stack policy that denies Update:Replace on the VPC, so CloudFormation adds the second range in place instead of replacing the resource
Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the VPC so the existing VPC stays and CloudFormation applies the new CidrBlock to it as an in-place update
Add a DeletionPolicy of Retain to the VPC so that CloudFormation keeps the old VPC while it creates the replacement VPC with both CIDR ranges

stem: An egress VPC uses AWS Network Firewall with strict rule order and the stateful default action Drop all. A stateful domain list rule group allows HTTPS to .partner-api.example with the TLS_SNI target type. After deployment, all outbound HTTPS fails, including to the allowed partner domain, and firewall logs (with Alert all enabled) show TCP SYN packets being dropped by the default action. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Change the domain list target type from TLS_SNI to HTTP_HOST, because Network Firewall inspects the Host header of HTTPS requests to find the domain
Set the stateless default action to Pass for port 443 traffic, so that HTTPS packets skip the stateful engine and reach the partner domain directly
Change the stateful default action to Drop established, so the TCP handshake can complete and the TLS SNI can be inspected against the allowlist
Move the domain allowlist into a stateless rule group with a higher priority, because stateless rules are evaluated before the stateful default action

stem: An API behind an Application Load Balancer is protected by an AWS WAF web ACL with the SQL database managed rule group. A penetration tester bypasses it by padding the JSON body with 9 KB of harmless data and placing a SQL injection payload after it. Legitimate API requests never exceed 4 KB. What is the most effective fix?

choices.text: Enable AWS Shield Advanced automatic application layer mitigation on the ALB, so AWS creates rules that block the padded requests during the attack
Add a rate-based rule that limits each client IP address to 100 requests per five minutes, so the tester cannot repeat the padding attack at a useful speed
Raise the web ACL's request body inspection limit to 64 KB, so the SQL database managed rule group inspects the full body of every request sent to the ALB
Add a rule that blocks requests whose body is larger than 8 KB, with oversize handling set to match, so padded requests are blocked before other rules run

stem: A Network Load Balancer created two years ago without security groups forwards TCP 443 to an EC2 fleet. To accept NLB traffic, the targets' security group allows TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0, and a scan shows the targets are reachable directly from other VPC resources. The security team wants targets to accept traffic only through the load balancer. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Create a new Network Load Balancer with a security group, move the listener and target group to it, and allow TCP 443 on targets only from that security group
Replace the targets' inbound rule with rules that reference the Network Load Balancer's network interfaces by ID, so only packets from those interfaces are allowed
Associate a new security group with the existing Network Load Balancer, then allow TCP 443 in the targets' security group only from that security group
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL with the Network Load Balancer and add rules that allow only requests sent through the load balancer's listener to reach the targets

stem: Engineers must SSH to Linux instances in private subnets that have no public IP addresses and no internet or NAT path. The security team wants no bastion hosts, no VPN clients, access controlled by IAM, and every connection attempt recorded in CloudTrail. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Deploy AWS Client VPN with certificate-based mutual authentication and authorize the engineers' group to reach the private subnets on TCP 22 only
Grant engineers IAM permission for the ec2-instance-connect:OpenTunnel action on the endpoint, optionally limited by the target port and private IP
Create an interface VPC endpoint for the com.amazonaws.region.ec2-instance-connect service and allow TCP 22 on the instances from the endpoint subnet
Allow inbound TCP 22 on the instances from the Region's EC2 Instance Connect managed prefix list so the service can open sessions from AWS addresses
Create an EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint in the VPC with its own security group, and allow TCP 22 on the instances only from that endpoint's security group

stem: After an incident, a security team must capture full packet contents, not only connection metadata, from 20 EC2 instances in a production VPC and feed them to a fleet of open-source IDS appliances. The production routing and application paths must not change, and only traffic on TCP 443 and 5432 should be analyzed. Which approach should the team implement?

choices.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs with a custom format that includes all available fields, deliver them to S3, and replay the flow records through the IDS appliances
Route the production subnets through an AWS Network Firewall endpoint with alert rules, and send the firewall's alert logs to the IDS appliances
Create Traffic Mirroring sessions on the instances' ENIs with a filter for TCP 443 and 5432, targeting a Network Load Balancer in front of the IDS fleet
Enable GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring on the 20 instances and export its findings, which include captured packet payloads, to the IDS appliances

stem: Workloads in a VPC call AWS Secrets Manager through an interface VPC endpoint whose policy allows only principals from the company's organization. The security team wants to see every request that passes through this endpoint, including requests signed with credentials from accounts outside the organization that the endpoint policy denied. Those denied calls do not appear in the team's CloudTrail management events. What should the team enable?

choices.text: CloudTrail data events for Secrets Manager secrets in the organization trail, because denied requests from outside principals are recorded as data events
VPC Flow Logs on the endpoint's network interfaces with the custom format, because the flow records include the caller account and the API action
Route 53 Resolver query logging on the VPC, because each call to the endpoint first resolves the service name and records the caller identity
CloudTrail network activity events for the Secrets Manager event source on a trail in the account that owns the VPC endpoint, filtering for denied calls

stem: A security team needs DNS query logs from every VPC in 50 member accounts delivered to one S3 bucket in a central log archive account, with the same configuration everywhere and the least setup in each member account. Which approach should the team use?

choices.text: Create a Resolver query logging configuration with the central S3 bucket as destination, share it through AWS RAM, and associate it with the member VPCs
Enable Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts and export its raw DNS query logs from the delegated administrator account to the central S3 bucket every hour
Create a Resolver query logging configuration in each member account with a local CloudWatch log group, and stream every group to Firehose and then S3
Enable VPC Flow Logs with a custom format in every VPC and deliver them to the central bucket, because flow records include the DNS query name for each lookup

stem: A team creates VPC Flow Logs that deliver directly to an S3 bucket. The bucket policy grants delivery.logs.amazonaws.com s3:PutObject with the required conditions, and default encryption uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key. The flow logs are created successfully, but no log files ever appear in the bucket. What is the most likely cause?

choices.text: Flow log records are buffered for 24 hours before delivery to S3, so the files will appear the next day once the first aggregation window has closed
Flow logs delivered to S3 need an IAM role that grants s3:PutObject, and the role was not provided, so the service has no permission to write the objects
The KMS key policy does not allow delivery.logs.amazonaws.com to use the key, so writing the encrypted objects fails even though the bucket policy allows it
Flow logs can be delivered only to S3 buckets that use SSE-S3 encryption, so the bucket must be switched away from SSE-KMS before any records can be written

stem: A web form served through CloudFront collects a national ID number, which is sent to an origin behind an ALB and passes through several microservices and logging layers. Only one backend verification service may ever see the plaintext value; every other component must see only ciphertext, even inside the VPC. What should the company implement?

choices.text: Set the viewer and origin protocol policies to HTTPS only and enable TLS from the ALB to all targets, so the national ID number is encrypted end to end
Configure CloudFront field-level encryption with a public key for the ID field, and keep the matching private key only in the verification service
Use a CloudFront Function to hash the ID field at the edge with SHA-256 before forwarding it, so that downstream services never see the original value
Enable mutual TLS on the ALB listener and issue client certificates to each microservice, so that only authenticated services can receive the form data

stem: An IoT platform runs an MQTT broker fleet on EC2 that listens with TLS on port 8883. Devices authenticate with client certificates that the brokers validate themselves, and the security policy requires that the TLS private key exist only on the broker instances. The company needs a load balancer in front of the fleet. Which configuration meets the requirements?

choices.text: A Network Load Balancer with a TLS listener on 8883 that uses an ACM certificate and forwards to a TLS target group so traffic is re-encrypted to the brokers
A Network Load Balancer with a TCP listener on 8883 that passes the TLS session through to the brokers, which complete the handshake and check certificates
An Application Load Balancer with mutual TLS in verify mode on port 8883, which forwards the validated client certificate to the brokers in request headers
A Gateway Load Balancer with a listener for port 8883 that forwards the encrypted MQTT sessions to the broker instances registered in its target group

stem: A CloudFront distribution uses an internet-facing ALB as its origin, with the origin domain set to the ALB's default DNS name. The ALB's HTTPS listener has an ACM certificate for app.example.com. After the origin protocol policy is changed to HTTPS only, all requests fail with HTTP 502. The distribution does not forward the viewer Host header. What should be done?

choices.text: Create an alias record such as origin.example.com for the ALB, add that name to the ALB certificate, and use it as the CloudFront origin domain name
Add TLSv1 to the origin SSL protocols on the distribution, because the ALB's default security policy negotiates older TLS versions that CloudFront rejects
Change the origin protocol policy to Match viewer, so that CloudFront keeps HTTPS for secure viewers but can fall back to HTTP when TLS to the origin fails
Increase the origin response timeout and keep-alive timeout on the origin, because TLS negotiation with the ALB takes longer than the default timeouts

stem: A company's security standard forbids pre-shared keys for IPsec. A new branch connects to a transit gateway with Site-to-Site VPN, and the branch router's public IP address is assigned dynamically by its ISP and can change. The company already runs AWS Private CA. How should the VPN authentication be implemented?

choices.text: Enable accelerated VPN on the connection, because the Global Accelerator edge authenticates the branch router by its anycast source address instead of a key
Create the customer gateway with the router's current IP address and update it through automation each time the ISP assigns a new public address to the router
Keep pre-shared keys but store them in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation every 30 days, so the keys are never visible to administrators
Issue a certificate for the router from AWS Private CA, create the customer gateway with that certificate's ARN, and configure the router with the certificate

stem: A company inspects all inter-VPC traffic in a central inspection VPC that has AWS Network Firewall endpoints in three Availability Zones. Spoke VPCs are attached to a transit gateway, and the spoke route tables send 0.0.0.0/0 to the inspection VPC attachment. Short-lived flows between two spokes work, but long TCP sessions between a client in one Availability Zone and a server in another Availability Zone are reset intermittently, and the stateful engine logs show only one direction of those flows. What should the network engineer change?

choices.text: Add a stateless rule group that forwards all traffic to the stateful engine so the engine can rebuild session state for flows that arrive out of order
Disable route propagation on the spoke attachments and replace the propagated routes with static routes that point at one firewall endpoint subnet
Turn on cross-zone load balancing for the firewall so any endpoint can accept return packets and share the flow state table with the other endpoints
Enable appliance mode on the transit gateway attachment of the inspection VPC so both directions of a flow use the same Availability Zone's firewall endpoint

stem: A centralized inspection VPC uses the CIDR 100.64.0.0/16 and inspects traffic for spoke VPCs in 10.0.0.0/8. A security engineer adds a Suricata-compatible stateful rule group with the rule alert http $HOME_NET any -> $EXTERNAL_NET any (http.host; content:"pastebin.example"; sid:1000001;). Test requests from spoke instances to that host are forwarded without any alert, although the same content in a rule that uses any as the source does alert. What is the most likely cause and fix?

choices.text: The rule group capacity was set too low, so Network Firewall silently skipped rules that were added after the capacity limit was reached
The alert action is evaluated only for stateless rule groups, so the rule must be moved into a stateless group and given the aws:forward_to_sfe action
The http keyword only inspects traffic that was decrypted first, so a TLS inspection configuration with a certificate from ACM has to be attached to the policy
HOME_NET defaults to the inspection VPC range, so spoke sources look external; override HOME_NET with the spoke CIDRs in the policy variables

stem: An internet-facing Application Load Balancer serves a website and a login page at /login. Each client IP address must be limited to 100 requests per 5 minutes on /login only, because normal browsing on other paths legitimately exceeds that rate. The team uses AWS WAF and wants the smallest change to the existing web ACL. Which rule should the engineer add?

choices.text: A regular rule that blocks requests to /login whose source address is not on an IP set reference statement that lists the known office ranges
A rate-based rule with a custom aggregation key on the URI path and a limit of 100, so that requests to /login are counted separately from other paths
A rate-based rule with the IP address aggregation key and a limit of 100 that has no scope-down statement, placed before all other rules in the web ACL
A rate-based rule with the IP address aggregation key, a limit of 100, and a scope-down statement that matches URI paths starting with /login

stem: A company provides employees with AWS Client VPN access. Users sign in through a SAML 2.0 identity provider and are members of the groups Finance and Engineering. Finance users may reach only the accounting database subnet 10.0.10.0/24, and Engineering users may reach only the build subnet 10.0.20.0/24. Both subnets are in the VPC that is associated with the endpoint. The company wants one Client VPN endpoint and the smallest possible configuration. What should the network engineer configure?

choices.text: One authorization rule per group, each with the destination CIDR of its subnet and the identity provider group ID as the access group
One route table entry for each subnet in the endpoint route table, with a target that names the identity provider group that may use the route
One authorization rule for the VPC CIDR that allows all users, plus security groups on the endpoint that permit only the subnet each group needs
A separate Client VPN endpoint for each group, each with a network ACL on the associated subnet that matches the users' assigned client CIDR range

stem: A company runs an internet-facing Application Load Balancer in a VPC with public subnets in two Availability Zones. A new policy requires that all inbound internet traffic is inspected by third-party firewall appliances in a Gateway Load Balancer target group before it reaches the load balancer, and that the appliances never receive traffic that skips the inspection path. Which design meets the requirement?

choices.text: Place a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint in each ALB subnet and add a route in the main route table that points 0.0.0.0/0 at the endpoint for both directions

Add Gateway Load Balancer endpoints in dedicated subnets, associate a route table with the internet gateway that sends each ALB subnet CIDR to the endpoint in its zone, and route returns back through it
Register the appliance instances as targets of the internet-facing Application Load Balancer and have listener rules forward each request to them before the application
Assign Elastic IP addresses to the appliances, publish those addresses in DNS instead of the ALB addresses, and let the appliances re-encrypt and forward requests to the load balancer

stem: A regulated company uses Amazon Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall in all VPCs to block resolution of domains on a curated deny list. The security policy says that if DNS Firewall cannot evaluate a query, for example during a service disruption, the query must not be answered without filtering, even if some applications temporarily fail to resolve names. Which configuration matches the policy?

choices.text: Set the fail-open setting to disabled in the DNS Firewall configuration of each VPC, and accept that queries may fail while the firewall is unavailable
Change every rule in the rule group to the BLOCK action with a NODATA response, so that queries that cannot be evaluated receive an empty answer
Enable DNSSEC validation on the VPC resolver, which makes Route 53 Resolver return no answer for any query that DNS Firewall has not evaluated
Enable the fail-open setting in the DNS Firewall configuration of each VPC so that queries continue and the deny list applies again when the firewall recovers

stem: A media company runs a public application on an Application Load Balancer and wants AWS Shield Advanced to engage the AWS Shield Response Team (SRT) proactively when an attack makes the application unhealthy, without waiting for the company to open a support case. Which TWO actions are required for proactive engagement to work? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Grant the SRT access to the AWS WAF web ACL logs in the Amazon S3 bucket that receives them
Turn on automatic application layer DDoS mitigation for the protected resource so that the SRT is added to the web ACL
Create an AWS Firewall Manager Shield Advanced policy so that the resource is tracked by the SRT
Provide emergency contact details in Shield Advanced that the SRT can use, and enable proactive engagement for the subscription
Associate an Amazon Route 53 health check that reflects the application's health with the protected Application Load Balancer resource in Shield Advanced

stem: A company shares one transit gateway among 25 accounts in an organization. Auditors ask for evidence of which VPC attachments exchanged traffic, including packets dropped because a route pointed to a blackhole, for all VPC-to-VPC and on-premises flows. The network team owns the transit gateway, but it cannot enable logs in each account's VPCs. Which solution gives the evidence with the least operational effort?

choices.text: Enable Traffic Mirroring on the transit gateway attachments and send the mirrored packets to a Network Load Balancer in the network account for later analysis
Create Transit Gateway flow logs on the gateway with custom fields for attachment IDs and dropped packet counters, and deliver them to Amazon S3
Enable AWS CloudTrail data events for the transit gateway so that every forwarded packet is recorded as an event in the organization trail
Create VPC Flow Logs on the transit gateway network interfaces in each attached VPC and aggregate them in the network account

stem: A security engineer sets up VPC Traffic Mirroring to feed an intrusion detection appliance. The source is the primary network interface of an instance on the Nitro system. The mirror target is a Network Load Balancer whose targets are the IDS instances, and the mirror filter accepts all inbound and outbound traffic. The session shows as active, yet the IDS instances receive no packets. The security group of the IDS instances allows TCP 22 from the management subnet and TCP 443 from the tools subnet only. What is the most likely reason?

choices.text: The mirror filter needs a separate rule for each protocol, because an accept-all rule is not applied to TCP and UDP traffic
Mirrored packets arrive VXLAN-encapsulated on UDP port 4789, and the IDS instances' security group does not allow that traffic
The source instance must have a VPC Flow Logs configuration before its interface can be a mirror source
Mirror targets can only be network interfaces of single instances, so a Network Load Balancer cannot be used as a mirror session destination

stem: A network engineer runs VPC Reachability Analyzer from an application instance to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance on port 5432. The analysis result is Reachable and shows the path through the instance security group, the route table and the database security group. Nevertheless, the application still times out when it connects to the database. What should the engineer conclude?

choices.text: Reachable results apply only to the ICMP protocol, so the engineer has to rerun the analysis with the TCP option to test port 5432
The analysis result is cached for 24 hours, so a recent security group change is missing and the analysis has to be started again after the cache expires
Reachability Analyzer skips network ACLs, so an ACL deny on the database subnet must be the cause and only VPC Flow Logs can reveal it
Reachability Analyzer only analyzes configuration and sends no packets, so check what it cannot see, such as a host firewall or a listener that is not accepting connections

stem: A team wants to log requests that AWS WAF blocks on an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, to keep the logs in Amazon S3 for audits, and to make sure Authorization header values never appear in the logs. An engineer creates a bucket named corp-waf-logs and tries to choose it as the logging destination of the web ACL, but the configuration is rejected. Which set of actions completes the requirement?

choices.text: Use a bucket whose name starts with aws-waf-logs-, add a logging filter that keeps BLOCK actions, and redact the Authorization header field
Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs in a log group with any name, then create a metric filter that removes the Authorization header value
Create an AWS CloudTrail trail with data events for the web ACL and store the events in the corp-waf-logs bucket with SSE-KMS
Enable S3 server access logging on the corp-waf-logs bucket and have the web ACL write its sampled requests to that bucket every five minutes for the audit

stem: A security team stores VPC Flow Logs from 200 VPCs in Amazon S3 as gzip-compressed text with the default format and no partitioning. Analysts use Amazon Athena to answer questions about a single day, but each query scans months of data and costs and run times keep growing. The team wants to cut the scanned data without changing how analysts write their SQL more than adding a date filter. Which change is the best fit?

choices.text: Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter that copies each record to an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain and query the domain instead of Athena
Publish new logs in Apache Parquet with Hive-compatible S3 prefixes and hourly partitions, and define the Athena table with partitions on the date and hour
Set a per-query data usage limit on the Athena workgroup so that any query that would scan more than a fixed amount of data is cancelled
Keep the text format and add an S3 Lifecycle rule that moves objects older than 30 days to S3 Glacier Deep Archive so that Athena skips them

stem: A security operations team supports 60 accounts in an AWS Organization. They need one central store that keeps VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 Resolver query logs and CloudTrail management events from all accounts and Regions in a common schema, so that several third-party security analytics tools can query the same data without building separate parsers. Which service should the team use?

choices.text: Amazon Security Lake with a delegated administrator, the log sources enabled for the organization, and a subscriber for each tool
AWS Config with a multi-account aggregator, using advanced queries to search the network logs that the aggregator collects
Amazon Detective, which stores the raw logs of every account and lets outside tools read them through a data-sharing API
Amazon CloudWatch Logs cross-account observability, with a Lambda parser for each source that converts every log to a shared schema

stem: A compliance team needs to know quickly when anyone turns off network visibility by deleting an AWS VPC Flow Logs configuration in a production account, and needs an ongoing check that every VPC has flow logs enabled. Which TWO mechanisms together meet the requirement? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A Network Access Analyzer scope that lists every VPC in the organization whose flow log configuration is deleted
A VPC Reachability Analyzer scheduled analysis that fails when a flow log configuration is no longer attached to the VPC
An Amazon CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the flow log group that raises an alarm when the volume of records reaches zero
An AWS Config managed rule that evaluates whether flow logs are enabled for each VPC, with findings reported through Config compliance
An Amazon EventBridge rule that matches the CloudTrail management event for DeleteFlowLogs and notifies an Amazon SNS topic

stem: A financial company publishes an API on an Application Load Balancer for about 30 partner banks. Each partner uses its own certificate authority, and the list of accepted authorities changes weekly through a workflow owned by the application team. The application must run its own validation logic, including partner-specific revocation checks, and must see the full client certificate. The ALB must still terminate TLS. Which ALB configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Configure the HTTPS listener with mutual authentication in passthrough mode, so the ALB forwards the client certificate chain to the targets in the X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert header
Configure the listener as a TCP listener without TLS termination, so the targets receive the client handshake and validate the certificate themselves
Configure the HTTPS listener with mutual authentication in verify mode, upload one trust store bundle to Amazon S3 and let the ALB reject any certificate that is not in it
Configure an authenticate-oidc action on the listener rule and require partners to present an ID token that carries the certificate subject as a claim

stem: A payment application uses an Application Load Balancer with an HTTPS listener that still has the security policy ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08. A PCI assessment requires that TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 be refused. Modern browsers should be able to use TLS 1.3, but the company also has point-of-sale terminals that only support TLS 1.2 and must keep working. Which security policy should the engineer select?

choices.text: ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS-1-2-2017-01, which accepts only TLS 1.2 and cannot negotiate TLS 1.3 sessions
ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-3-2021-06, which accepts only TLS 1.3 and refuses every earlier protocol version
ELBSecurityPolicy-2016-08, which accepts TLS 1.0 through TLS 1.2 and adds TLS 1.3 in the newest software release
ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06, which accepts TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 and refuses older protocol versions

stem: A company has a 1 Gbps hosted AWS Direct Connect connection to a transit gateway through a transit virtual interface. Policy requires that the traffic on the connection is encrypted with IPsec and that no public IP addresses are used for the tunnels, because the connection is a private path. MACsec is not available on this connection. Which TWO actions build the solution? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Create a Site-to-Site VPN on a public virtual interface and connect the tunnels to the public IP addresses of the customer gateway device
Create a Site-to-Site VPN attachment on the transit gateway with a private IPv4 outside address type, using the Direct Connect gateway attachment as its transport
Enable MACsec on the hosted connection by requesting the CKN and CAK through the Direct Connect console
Attach a virtual private gateway to the VPC, associate it with a private virtual interface and create a private IP VPN on that gateway
Configure a CIDR block on the transit gateway to provide the private IP addresses that AWS uses for the tunnel endpoints of the VPN

stem: A security auditor reviews an Application Load Balancer that has an HTTPS listener and an HTTPS target group. The targets present self-signed certificates, and one of them expired three weeks ago. Users are not affected: the ALB keeps forwarding requests to all targets and health checks still pass. The auditor asks why the ALB has not rejected the expired certificate. What is the correct explanation and action?

choices.text: The ALB skipped the certificate check because health checks use HTTP; switching the health check protocol to HTTPS would enforce validation for the traffic too
The ALB validates target certificates only against ACM certificates in its Region, so self-signed ones pass because they postdate the listener certificate
The ALB encrypts traffic to targets but never validates the target certificate's chain, expiry or name, so backend identity needs other controls
The ALB automatically renews expired self-signed certificates on its targets through an ACM integration, so the expiry has no effect on the connection

stem: A security team wants to guarantee that data in an Amazon S3 bucket is accessed only over TLS 1.2 or later, and that older clients that still negotiate TLS 1.0 or 1.1 or use plain HTTP are refused rather than merely reported. The bucket is accessed from VPCs through a gateway endpoint and from the internet. Which control enforces this?

choices.text: A bucket policy statement with a Deny effect only for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, which also blocks all TLS versions older than 1.2 by design
A gateway endpoint policy that allows access to the bucket only when the aws:SourceVpce value matches, which limits access to TLS 1.2 clients
An AWS Config rule for S3 buckets that requires SSL requests and marks the bucket noncompliant when TLS 1.0 is used, so the objects are then blocked
Bucket policy Deny statements for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false and for requests where s3:TlsVersion is numerically less than 1.2

stem: A company exposes an Amazon API Gateway REST API to partners. A custom domain name api.example.com is configured with mutual TLS and a truststore in Amazon S3, and partners that use the custom domain must present certificates. A security test shows that a client without any certificate can still call the API by using the default https://abc123.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com URL. What should the company do to close the gap?

choices.text: Add the partner certificates to the API's resource policy so that API Gateway checks them on the default endpoint
Disable the default execute-api endpoint so clients can reach the API only through the mutual TLS custom domain name
Attach an AWS WAF web ACL to the stage with a rule that blocks requests for the default execute-api host name
Change the custom domain endpoint type to edge-optimized, which applies the S3 truststore to the default endpoint as well
